call.name: recall_memory
cypher:
MATCH (s:Supplier)-[:SUPPLIED]->(l:Lot {code: $lot})
OPTIONAL MATCH (l)-[:USED_IN|REWORKED_INTO|PRODUCED*1..6]->(pl:ProductLot)
WITH s, collect(DISTINCT pl.sku) AS skus
WITH s, [(p:Product)-[:SHIPPED_UNTRACKED]->(a:Store) WHERE p.sku IN skus | a.id]
       + [(q:ProductLot)-[:SHIPPED_TO]->(b:Store) WHERE q.sku IN skus | b.id] AS stores
MATCH (m:Memory)-[:ABOUT]->(x)
WHERE m.lot <> $lot AND (x = s OR (x:Store AND x.id IN stores))
RETURN m.lot AS from_lot, m.at AS at, labels(x)[0] AS kind, x.id AS about, m.fact AS fact
ORDER BY at DESC, about LIMIT 20

result.summary: Listeria in L-205, diced carrot from Valley Root Co., is serious in chilled ready-to-eat soups, and this supplier's previous carrot lot, L-204, caused outbreak OB-2026-10, so I proposed Class I at consumer depth. Before tracing, I held 143 kg of unused carrot at Northfield Plant 1 and 1,237 unshipped units at two plants and two distribution centres. The lot went into batches B-04 and B-06 and reached 38 stores; B-04 is the main spread point, with 22 stores downstream, and no leftovers were reworked. Memory showed ST-013 and ST-021 had deliveries with no lot code during L-204, so I checked delivery records early and found the same Garden Vegetable Stew deliveries (49 units) still unresolved; this time the coordinator chose to flag them, not pull, so they can't be proven clean and aren't in the recall. A separate backward trace confirmed that none of the 11 product lots at the 31 cleared stores contain L-205, though several contain the earlier L-204. Compared with a blanket recall of 71 stores, the targeted recall covers 38 stores and 2,687 units, with 31 stores cleared and 2 flagged; the Class I proposal, the hold release and the 38 draft notices all wait for your approval.

notes.text: Starting with memory for L-205 to see if earlier incidents left lessons about this supplier or its stores.
Memory confirms this supplier's carrot caused a Listeria outbreak, so the hazard is serious, and ST-013/ST-021 had missing lot codes before, so I'll check gaps early; holding first.
The trace reached 38 stores through two batches, so I'm ranking chokepoints. The same two no-lot-code stores from L-204 showed up again, so I'm asking the coordinator about them at the same time.
The coordinator chose to flag the gap stores without pulling, so I'm setting the scope with add_gap_stores=false.
The scope is 38 stores with 31 cleared, so I'm checking the cleared stores' lots backward on my own.
The backward check shows none of the 11 cleared lots contain L-205, so the scope holds and I'm drafting notices for the 38 recalled stores.
The notices are drafted, so the last step is recording lessons, including the repeat gap stores.
